parsed.explanation: Combined regime pairs national binary document/entry rules with a state facility ban covering government buildings, schools, universities, airports, parks and detention sites, enforceable as criminal trespass after refusal to leave. Entry discrepancy can trigger refusal and, if wilful material misrepresentation is found, lifetime fraud ineligibility, though not automatic. One documented arrest, 60-day maximum, 24 hours in men's ward, then dismissal on standing; no routine imprisonment or execution. Courts have blocked some national orders and care bans, private businesses are outside the state ban, and counties covering about 55% of population add protections. Universal government-facility and document exposure, thin state recourse, minor-care/school restrictions and hostile official framing keep the case in Elevated Risk, mitigated by functioning courts and limited enforcement.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary passport rule stops X/non-matching markers; entry cable directs refusal for document discrepancy or doubt about sex and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for wilful material misrepresentation. State licences/birth certificates cannot match birth sex, treated as fraud for residents.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers possible. Passport suit pending; several executive orders blocked or enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor's home passport is checked nationally at entry before state systems; a mismatch can escalate from secondary screening to refusal, then state facility/document rules if admitted.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Document discrepancy can prompt detention/questioning; state trespass arrest held arrestee 24 hours in men's ward. National prison policy from 2026 removes hormones and imposes psychiatric treatment; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse for trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires wilful entry plus refusal to leave when asked, with exemptions; the sole documented case was dismissed 20 June 2025 on standing. No documented routine visitor imprisonment.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility encounter can become trespass arrest, then birth-sex ward placement; entry fraud allegation can move visitor into immigration detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State 2023 law bars restrooms/changing facilities consistent with gender identity in all government-owned/leased buildings, schools public and private in purported scope, universities, airports, parks, toll plazas, prisons/jails. National order bars government-funded facilities congruent with identity.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses are outside state scope; counties/cities covering about 55% of population prohibit discrimination in public accommodations. Exemptions cover emergencies, child/elderly/disability assistance, out-of-order facilities and others.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National and state bans overlap in government/airport settings with no documented pre-emption; private-sector access does not cancel airport/government exposure.

care_services.exposure: State bans hormone/puberty/surgical care for minors, 24-hour wait and insurance/physician-only barriers for adults, conscience refusals; national orders restrict minor care and public insurance. Ward placement by document marker can delay or misplace care.
care_services.protection: A national judge permanently blocked provisions banning care for minors and adults in June 2024, after earlier preliminary injunction and stay; current appellate status is unresolved. Emergency care not documented as denied.
care_services.interaction: A minor travelling with a guardian faces school, facility and care restrictions together; adult hormone continuity can be disrupted by physician-only and insurance rules.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders define sex as binary at birth, remove gender-identity policies, direct investigation/prosecution over school social transition, and counterterrorism documents use 'radical gender ideology'/'radically pro-transgender' framing. State facility law treats identity-consistent use as trespass if refused to depart.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2020 national employment ruling and national hate-crimes statute cover gender identity; several orders enjoined; state human-relations commission enforces the 2020 ruling since 2021.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing supports facility and school enforcement but has not, in this dossier, produced documented visitor sweeps or capital charges; courts remain a partial check.

minors_guardians.exposure: School facility ban, exclusion from female school sports by birth sex, minor care ban, national directive to criminally investigate teachers facilitating social transition including pronouns. Parent custody can be modified where child receives or might receive gender-affirming care under national/state laws.
minors_guardians.protection: Care bans were blocked by a national judge in June 2024 with unresolved appeal status; drag/live-performance ban preliminarily enjoined; no documented visitor family detention in this dossier.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces combined school/restroom, sports, care and custody-rule exposure; a guardian may face investigation or loss of custody recognition across state lines.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A law-versus-violence analysis reports 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k per year and labels the state 'Do Not Travel', while finding overall law severity does not correlate with killing rates. National advocacy travel advisories in 2023 cited health, safety and freedom risks and event cancellations.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity, but state hate-crime law covers sexual orientation not gender identity; local protections cover about 55% of population. No documented state-directed street sweeps against visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence figure is documented without a clear general homicide comparator in the dossier, so it is counted proportionally, not as an organised campaign; thin state recourse increases street risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: State has no employment/housing anti-discrimination statute covering gender identity; remedies for facility arrest were not substantively tested because dismissal was on standing. Passport, executive-order and care litigation remains unresolved and travel-time status can change.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit on passport markers, injunctions against several orders, human-relations commission enforcement, and local ordinances provide partial recourse. Legal-aid FAQ guidance exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists mainly through national courts and local ordinances, not state facilities or hate-crime law; the traveller may need to leave before slow remedies conclude.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that police can detain for identity/facility noncompliance and impose fines or short custody with slow remedies; higher than 0.35 because detention is not routine or extortionate, private businesses are exempt, the only arrest was dismissed, and national courts have blocked several measures.

Closest: routine document/facility exposure, documented detention and humiliation, denial or disruption of care, custodial sentences unlikely, courts recognise narrow claims but remedies are slow. This case is slightly lower due to criminal trespass, men's-ward holding, entry fraud consequences and minor restrictions.

Higher than 0.55 because secondary screening is not merely administrative delay: government-facility exclusion is universal in the state, trespass carries jail, and document discrepancy can support refusal and possible lifetime ineligibility, with no state anti-discrimination backstop.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one combined system: national entry/document screening first, then state government-facility, school, university and airport rules, with birth-sex custody or ward placement if detention occurs. Protections are real but partial and mostly external to the state ban: national courts, local ordinances, private-business exemption and narrow trespass elements. The harshest operative rules govern: universal government-facility exclusion and document mismatch exposure, tempered by rare documented arrest, no execution or routine imprisonment, and active litigation. That places the combined regime below administrative-friction anchors and above routine-detention anchors.
